books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Presidential election results, November 4, 1856. Figures from the American Presidency Project (presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/elections/1856); 296 electoral votes in all, 149 needed to win. Fillmore carried only Maryland.
stimulus.text:
| Candidate | Party | Popular votes | Share | Electoral votes |
| James Buchanan | Democratic | 1,836,072 | 45.3% | 174 |
| John C. Frémont | Republican | 1,342,345 | 33.1% | 114 |
| Millard Fillmore | American (Know-Nothing) | 873,053 | 21.5% | 8 |

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: Fillmore’s showing in the table best illustrates that in 1856

options.text: the old Whig Party had returned to power.
options.misconception: Background from the books: the Whigs had dissolved by 1856; Fillmore ran for the American Party, not the Whigs.

options.text: the Democrats had lost their hold on the South.
options.misconception: Buchanan won every slave state except Maryland; the Democrats held the South.

options.text: nativism still drew a fifth of the vote.
Frémont had carried the slave states of the South.
options.misconception: Frémont won no slave state; his 114 electoral votes came from the free states.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the Whigs had dissolved by 1856; Fillmore ran for the American Party, not the Whigs.
rationales.B: Buchanan won every slave state except Maryland; the Democrats held the South.
rationales.C: Fillmore, the American Party’s candidate, still won 21.5 percent of the popular vote, about a fifth.
rationales.D: Frémont won no slave state; his 114 electoral votes came from the free states.
rationales.general:
1. Find Fillmore’s row: 873,053 votes, 21.5 percent, 8 electoral votes.
2. Note his party: the American Party, the Know-Nothings, running on nativism.
3. See the point: even as slavery split the country, nativism still drew a fifth of the voters.
4. Note the geography: Fillmore’s only electoral votes came from Maryland, the one slave state he carried.
Remember: a third party’s vote share tells you what else voters cared about besides the main quarrel.
